item.title: [hackernews] Show HN: An e-ink frame that hears birds and draws them as 1800s illustrations
item.description: A Show HN project: an e-ink picture frame that listens for nearby bird calls and renders the birds it hears as 1800s-style illustrations. The linked page isn't summarized here; details beyond the title aren't available, so this is mainly a pointer for people curious about e-ink hardware, birdsong recognition, or generative image tricks.

item.title: [github_trending] cloudflare/security-audit-skill
item.description: cloudflare/security-audit-skill turns a coding agent into a security auditor, orchestrating isolated agents through six phases: reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification and target-neutral reporting. It is the single-repo skill that seeded Cloudflare's fleet-wide vulnerability discovery harness, and it writes independently verified, machine-readable findings to files like findings.json. Security teams building automated vulnera

item.title: [producthunt] tiun.
item.description: tiun. is a Product Hunt launch pitched at AI builders, bundling authentication, billing and payments so teams don't have to build login and subscription logic themselves. It targets indie developers and small teams that need to monetize an AI app quickly, though the listing gives no further detail on supported payment providers or pricing models.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: A developer recounts moving from Cursor to OpenAI Codex: after about a year on Cursor, starting with a $20/month personal plan in April 2025, his company switched its China region to Codex in April 2026, partly because Cursor moved from fixed licensing to usage-based billing that made costs higher and less predictable. His main takeaway is a difference in form: Cursor reads as an IDE with AI attached, while Codex feels closer to a general-purpose agent.

item.title: [zhihu] 如何看待 HYROX 失禁选手就北京赛场事件道歉，决定追溯性退出该场比赛，并放弃此前获得的积分？
item.description: A HYROX athlete who soiled themselves during the Beijing race has apologized, decided to retroactively withdraw from that event and give up the points earned there, according to a Zhihu question discussing the case. The thread centers on how far retroactive penalties should go and on the public pressure behind the apology; the linked page isn't summarized here, so details beyond the title aren't available.

The takeaway is that Claude is being pushed to tie together office-style workflows and compete with Microsoft's office ecosystem. Only the headline is available, so the exact product form and features aren't clear.

item.title: [v2ex] [Claude] 同一个账号，用不同的卡充值，会有问题吗？
item.description: A V2EX user asks whether the same Claude account can be topped up with different payment cards — one person's credit card in the first month, another person's debit card in the second. The concern is whether mixing cardholders and card types on a single account triggers fraud checks or a ban. The post only poses the question; no answers or test results are included.

item.title: [36kr] 8点1氪丨时隔三年多，美联储宣布加息25个基点；钟薛高降价重启，售价6.9元起；韩国“尸皮针”已在中国成立公司6年
item.description: 36Kr's '8点1氪' roundup covers three items: the Federal Reserve raising rates by 25 basis points after more than three years, the ice cream brand Zhongxuegao relaunching at lower prices starting from 6.9 yuan, and a Korean 'corpse-skin needle' business that has operated in China for six years. Only the headline digest is available, so the background and details can't be confirmed.

item.title: [v2ex] [Wunder] 当 Fable 和 Astra 可以看到对方的工作成果并且可以对话
item.description: A V2EX user shared a session in which two AI assistants, Fable and Astra, work on the same codebase: Fable reports a layout fix shipped, Astra flags a mobile tab-key navigation issue, notes iPhone supports external keyboards and that VoiceOver hits the same ordering problem, and the human decides to fix it. It is a concrete look at two models seeing each other's output and debating a bug, useful for anyone tracking multi-agent coding workflows.

item.title: [infoq] 实测 Vibe Key：开口使唤 AI，真有当甲方的感觉
item.description: Vibe Key, launched by Ulanzi and Tencent WorkBuddy, is a 269-299 yuan hardware mic with one microphone, three buttons and a knob; press it to wake WorkBuddy and dictate a task instead of typing prompts. InfoQ's hands-on review used it to generate a Mid-Autumn Festival poster and tested transcription in noisy environments, aimed at people who want a faster way to direct AI.

item.title: [github_trending] alibaba/open-code-review
item.description: Alibaba has open-sourced OpenCodeReview, a Go code-review tool that combines deterministic pipelines with an LLM agent to produce precise line-level comments, supported by a built-in multi-language ruleset covering issues such as NPEs and thread safety. It is described as battle-tested at Alibaba's scale, making it worth a look for teams wiring automated review into CI without trusting an LLM for every judgement.

item.title: [producthunt] Naoma AI Demo Agent V2
item.description: Naoma AI Demo Agent V2, newly listed on Product Hunt, is pitched as a way to turn website traffic into booked, qualified meetings. That puts it in the category of tools for B2B teams that treat their site as a lead source and want visitors pushed straight to a scheduled call; the listing itself offers no further detail.

item.title: [producthunt] Voiskey
item.description: Voiskey is an AI voice-typing tool listed on Product Hunt that claims its dictation “sounds right in every app”. Beyond that single-line description, the listing gives no supported platforms, pricing or underlying model, so anyone looking for cross-app dictation will have to try it to judge.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] Youtube 视频转成文字的阅读的小工具，优化了一些用户体验
item.description: The author updated a small tool that turns YouTube videos into readable articles, fixing three issues users raised: it now uses ASR to handle videos without subtitles, processes audio in chunks with live progress display to speed things up, and supports multiple output languages instead of Chinese only. The post invites both new and returning users to try it again.

item.title: [infoq] 亚马逊 CTO 要来中国了，说实话，这比泛滥的 AI 发布会值得关注
item.description: InfoQ reports that Amazon CTO Werner Vogels is coming to China. In his 14th and final re:Invent keynote in December 2025 he released no new products, instead proposing a "renaissance developer" framework with five traits: end-to-end ownership, systems thinking, extreme curiosity, deliberate AI use and storytelling. The piece notes he remains Amazon's VP and CTO as of September 2026 and still writes monthly on All Things Distributed.

item.title: [producthunt] Kilo Code for iOS and Android
item.description: Kilo Code has shipped iOS and Android apps that let you start coding agents, control sessions, and review pull requests from a phone. It moves the agent workflow beyond the desktop, which matters for developers who want to check progress or handle reviews while away from their machine.

item.title: [v2ex] [推广] Google one pro18 个月 Jio 渠道有货 最新价格 0.84u
item.description: A V2EX seller is promoting Google One Pro 18-month subscriptions activated through the Jio channel at $0.84, with single-unit orders handled via a Telegram bot or the ktno.cc shop and bulk pricing available on request. It targets people who want cheap Google One storage, though buyers have to judge the account and channel risks themselves.

item.title: [v2ex] [程序员] typeless 的每周额度降级到 2k 词,会员开不太起，有啥平替吗
item.description: A developer says typeless, a voice-input tool they rate highly, has cut its weekly quota to 2k words while the annual membership costs $139, so they are asking V2EX for cheaper alternatives. Their complaint is that most of the cost goes to LLM providers, making the subscription hard to justify.

item.title: [v2ex] [生活] 我的三十岁，以及从龟到独立人格的改变
item.description: A developer's personal essay written a month after turning thirty, tracing a childhood raised by his grandparents with parents he describes as NPD, then a software engineering degree, years at a provincial-city company before joining a subsidiary of a first-tier-city firm, and a home bought at the market peak whose down payment is gone. It is an honest look at family dynamics and life after thirty, aimed at readers who care about upbringing and the everyday reality of being a programmer.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] czlmail - 用 claude 写了个 jmap 的开源邮件客户端, 配合 stalwart 使用
item.description: czlmail is an open-source JMAP email client built with Wails and written with help from Claude, designed to work with Stalwart. Its basics follow Bulwark: mail, calendar, contacts and WebDAV files, plus extras such as WebDAV template sync, system notifications, AI integration and MCP support. It ships under AGPL-3.0 and the macOS build is still untested.

item.title: [v2ex] [OpenAI] ChatGPT 头一次遇到丢对话的情况
item.description: A V2EX user reports ChatGPT losing two of their conversations for the first time: both plain English-translation chats still appear in history, but opening them returns a no-access error. The real worry is that an important chat could become unopenable, since AI conversations are harder to back up than cloud files and even a local export would lose context.

item.description: A V2EX user has released a self-made text-based deduction game, 《以日为鉴：失落三十年》, in which players make choices starting from the peak of the 1989 bubble; the author says the maximum score is 60 points. item.description: LinkedIn has detailed the training infrastructure behind its AI-driven job search: a multi-teacher distillation pipeline that compresses an 8B relevance teacher and a 1.7B engagement teacher into a 600M-parameter ranking model, lifting NDCG@10 from 0.7583 to 0.9432. To keep iteration fast, the team serves the teachers inside the training loop via SGLang and adds an offline mode that precomputes teacher outputs, plus FSDP2 and H200 clusters for roughly 8x faster training overall. It is in product

The listing gives no further detail on supported models, features or pricing, so specifics require the linked page.

item.title: [infoq] 如何从历史中学习？基于RhymeRL的强化学习系统优化实践｜QCon上海
item.description: At QCon Shanghai, Shanghai Jiao Tong University associate professor Du Dongdong will present RhymeRL, built for LLM reinforcement learning where rollout dominates runtime and long tails leave the earliest-finished GPU idle roughly 76% of the time. Exploiting matchable tokens across adjacent epochs, it pairs historical speculative decoding with length scheduling plus offline suffix trees and reward-aware branch selection, reporting a 2.6x speedup over existing systems. It targets engineers optimi

item.title: [infoq] vivo 把 Agent 做进操作系统：6000 多项原子技能开放调用，AgentOS 预览版亮相
item.description: At its September 16 developer conference in Shenzhen, vivo unveiled OriginOS 7 and Blue River OS 4 and previewed AgentOS, which pushes agents into the OS layer. Its BlueLM Harness turns more than 6,000 atomic skills into agent-callable tools covering over 10,000 tasks, paired with on-device BlueLM-Nano and the BlueLM-RealTime speech model; BlueLM Xiaowei V Pro can now break down and run cross-app tasks. Relevant to developers building on-device agents.

item.title: [producthunt] Elva
item.description: Elva is a new Product Hunt listing whose only description is the tagline "Goodbye, Postman. Your APIs have new consumers," suggesting it targets teams looking for an alternative in the API tooling space. Beyond that line, the submission gives no further details on features, pricing, or how it differs from existing tools.

item.title: [infoq] 亚马逊云科技服务越做越多，Terraform Provider 正在变成关键“翻译层”
item.description: Terraform AWS Provider shipped v6.62.0 in August 2026, adding list resources plus resources for Amazon DSQL, ECS, ECR, SES and Pinpoint, and enhancing Bedrock AgentCore, CloudFront, ElastiCache and others. The article argues that as AWS's service catalog balloons, the provider is shifting from provisioning EC2 and S3 into an abstraction layer linking AWS APIs to infrastructure-as-code practice, and warns teams to pin, test and stage upgrades after v6.57.0 was retracted.

item.title: [producthunt] Hello Inbox
item.description: Hello Inbox is a Product Hunt launch whose stated goal is getting more marketing emails into the inbox rather than the spam folder. It is aimed at teams running email marketing campaigns, but the listing gives only that one line, with no detail on how it works or what it costs.

item.title: [infoq] 阶跃发布全新语音大模型 StepAudio 3系列：覆盖语音识别、生成、实时交互与音乐创作
item.description: 阶跃 launched the StepAudio 3 family on September 15 with five models — Realtime, ASR, TTS, Gen and Music — spanning live voice interaction, speech recognition, lifelike speech generation and music creation. Realtime does native full-duplex dialogue and tops Artificial Analysis's Conversational Dynamics and Speech Reasoning leaderboards with a 98.9% score, while ASR reaches a 1.7% word error rate, tied for first. Aimed at teams building full-stack voice products.

item.title: [infoq] 边说话边推理、边聊天边调用工具，谷歌 Gemini 3.8 Live 要攻克语音 Agent 的沉默时刻
item.description: Google released Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, two real-time conversational models now available through the Gemini API and Google AI Studio. The former targets low latency and scale, while Extended Thinking adds background reasoning: it can call tools asynchronously, say "let me check that" first and then report progress, so developers must read the Live API's IN_PROGRESS and IDLE states to know when a turn truly ends. Both also accept visual input.

It argues against Tokenmaxxing — judging engineers by token consumption — noting usage swings tenfold for the same person and tool, and that token spend shows no direct correlation with product value.

item.description: In a Lawfare essay, Bruce Schneier and Cindy Cohn trace how post-9/11 US surveillance shifted from targeted wiretaps and pen register orders to mass collection of internet backbone traffic and phone or internet metadata. item.title: [github_trending] Tencent/BrowserSkill
item.description: BrowserSkill, a Tencent open-source project, is a bsk CLI plus browser extension that lets shell-capable agents such as Cursor, Claude Code and Codex borrow tabs from your already logged-in browser, running the task in a separate visible Agent Window and returning the tab when finished. It keeps your real session and locks you into no particular model or agent framework, which suits anyone automating sites that require a live login.

item.title: [github_trending] affaan-m/ECC
item.description: ECC, a trending GitHub repository, describes itself as an agent harness performance optimization system for AI coding tools including Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, and Cursor. It bundles skills, instincts, memory, security, and a research-first development workflow into a unified, optimizable runtime. Developers who rely on multiple coding agents may find it useful for standardizing and hardening their setups.

item.title: [github_trending] Tencent/WeKnora
item.description: WeKnora is Tencent's open-source LLM knowledge platform that turns raw documents into a queryable RAG pipeline, an autonomous reasoning agent, and a self-maintaining wiki. It ships a Chrome extension plus WeChat dialog-platform and ClawHub integrations, so teams that want document Q&A and agentic retrieval can adopt it without assembling the stack themselves.

item.title: [juejin] 2026编程圈很火的10个Skills
item.description: This post rounds up ten "Skills" for AI coding assistants, built on Anthropic's Agent Skills standard from October 2025, where a workflow is written as a SKILL.md file that drops into ~/.claude/skills/ and loads automatically. As of July 2026 GitHub hosts more than 1,400 Claude Code Skills, but a test the author cites found 70% of 100 community Skills failing, which makes this filtered list the useful part.

item.title: [hackernews] A single firm is behind OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta hacking scandals
item.description: A Hacker News submission claims a single company is behind the hacking scandals tied to OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta. The submitted blurb identifies it as Irregular, described as an Israeli Effective Altruist firm, and says it caused unsecured AI models to hack real targets. No sources or further details are given.

item.title: [hackernews] An update on Wayback Machine access
item.description: In a September 15 blog post, the Internet Archive's Mark Graham explains the recent Wayback Machine failures: waves of high-volume automated traffic forced new protections, and the 429 "too many requests" block message was rewritten. Those protections sometimes catch real users by mistake, so anyone wrongly blocked can email info@archive.org with their OS, browser and IP address.

item.title: [hackernews] Training a 4B model to produce 81% faster query plans than Postgres
item.description: The write-up is about using agentic reinforcement learning to teach Qwen query optimization, training a 4B model whose query plans come out 81% faster than Postgres. Only the title and a one-line subtitle are available, so details on the training setup, datasets and evaluation aren't provided.

item.description: OpenResearch is a local-first workspace from alphaXiv that turns coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Cursor into research agents able to review literature, develop hypotheses, run experiments and produce research artifacts. Binaries are offered as a macOS dmg and a Windows CLI zip. It is aimed at developers and research teams that want their existing agents to cover the research workflow.

item.title: [hackernews] Mistral X Mozilla: Private, Multilingual AI Browsing
item.description: Mistral and Mozilla are teaming up to bring open, private, and multilingual AI into the web browser, putting trustworthy AI where people already browse. It's a development worth watching for developers and users who care about privacy and multilingual support in AI tooling.

item.title: [github_trending] NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra
item.description: Ghidra is a software reverse engineering framework built and maintained by the National Security Agency's Research Directorate. It bundles disassembly, decompilation, graphing and scripting for Windows, macOS and Linux binaries across many processor instruction sets, and runs both interactively and in automated mode. Users can extend it with Java or Python, making it a customizable platform for malware analysis and large-team SRE work.

item.title: [github_trending] JustVugg/colibri
item.description: colibri is a pure-C, dependency-free inference engine that treats disk, RAM and VRAM as one memory hierarchy and streams experts from disk, letting frontier MoE models of 744B to 2.8T parameters run on consumer or heterogeneous hardware. Nine model families are supported today, including GLM, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4. It targets developers who want to serve very large MoE models on machines they already own.

item.title: [github_trending] addyosmani/agent-skills
item.description: addyosmani/agent-skills packages the workflows, quality gates and best practices senior engineers rely on into "skills" that AI coding agents follow, spanning six phases from DEFINE and PLAN through BUILD, VERIFY and REVIEW to SHIP. It ships 9 slash commands such as /spec, /plan, /build and /test mapped to those stages, aimed at developers who want agents to apply engineering standards consistently.

item.title: [juejin] 白嫖DeepSeek V4 Pro！免费无限用，还能接入Claude-Code
item.description: A Juejin tutorial lays out five steps for using DeepSeek V4 Pro for free locally: register on ZenMux, create a PAYG API Key, restrict it to free models such as deepseek-v4-pro-free and deepseek-v4-flash-free, then plug the key into cc switch or Cherry Studio. The author says flash-free suits light tasks while pro-free handles coding and complex reasoning, but notes that in his own test the model replied it was not actually DeepSeek-v4.
